the existing models showing the relation between atmospheric visibility and free space optical link attenuation do not match with the field data.
the existing model for free space optical links attenuation has been modified to fit experimental data.
the Kruse model is modified to fit the data and a new model is derived.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the experimental measurement of the optical attenuation of a free space link as a function of atmospheric visibility.
the experimental investigation of the optical link attenuation for a free space optical communication system operating with a 0.78 μm wavelength and visibilities ranging from (9 to 12) km.
the development and validation of a model that can accurately estimate the attenuation in a terrestrial free space link as a function of visibility.

the proposed model can be used for the design of free space optics systems operating at a wavelength of 780 nm.
